slides.0.title: Course Introduction
slides.0.content:
Touraine is the Loire's most diverse sub-region for red and rosé wines. Beyond the famous Chinon and Bourgueil, Touraine offers a kaleidoscope of styles — from the Cot (Malbec) uniqueness of Touraine-Amboise to the intriguing Pineau d'Aunis-based rosé of Touraine-Noble-Joué. This lesson maps the full panorama of Touraine's red wine appellations.

AOCs Covered in This Lesson

Touraine (red/rosé), Touraine-Amboise (red), Touraine-Noble-Joué
slides.1.title: Touraine Red Wine Panorama
slides.1.content:
🍷 Touraine (Rouge / Rosé)

The broad regional AOC covering the entire Touraine sub-region. Permitted red grapes: Gamay (dominant), Cabernet Franc, Cot (Malbec), Pineau d'Aunis. Wines are light, fresh, fruit-forward — excellent value. Best drunk young at 13–15°C. Touraine rosé is dry to off-dry, salmon-colored, versatile with food.

🏰 Touraine-Amboise (Rouge)

Located around the town of Amboise, famous for its royal château. The world's only AOC requiring 100% Cot (Malbec) for red wines. Deep purple-ruby color, plum and blackberry fruit, violet hints — more body than Loire Cabernet Franc but retains Loire freshness. Can age 5–10 years. A unique expression of Malbec utterly different from Cahors or Argentina.

🌹 Touraine-Noble-Joué

A tiny appellation producing only rosé wine. A unique blend of three Pinot varieties: Pinot Meunier (dominant), Pinot Noir, and Pinot Gris. The resulting rosé is pale, delicate, with red fruit and floral character — sometimes called the "grey rosé" of the Loire. Only about 30 producers; one of France's rarest rosé styles.
slides.2.title: Quiz
slides.2.questions.0.question: Which AOC is covered in this lesson?
slides.2.questions.0.explanation: Touraine (red/rosé) is the broad regional Loire AOC covering reds and rosés from the Touraine sub-region. Dominated by Gamay, it offers fresh, fruit-forward wines at excellent value. Touraine-Amboise (requiring 100% Cot) and Touraine-Noble-Joué (unique three-Pinot rosé blend) complete the lesson.
